nodes.summary: A cache event over a type $\alpha$ of blocks records how one request is served: either a hit on the requested block $r \in \alpha$, or a miss on the requested block $r$ together with an optional evicted block $v \in \alpha$, absent when nothing is evicted.
nodes.title: Cache events

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity and suppose a finite sequence of cache events leads from the cache $C$ to the cache $C'$ by legal cache transitions for capacity $k$. If $C$ has no duplicate entries and length at most $k$, then $C'$ has no duplicate entries and length at most $k$.
nodes.title: Legal cache traces preserve valid caches

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity and let $C \to C'$ be a legal cache transition for capacity $k$, labelled by any cache event. If $C$ has no duplicate entries and length at most $k$, then $C'$ has no duplicate entries and length at most $k$.
nodes.title: Legal cache transitions preserve valid caches

nodes.summary: For a capacity $k \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the labelled transition system whose states are lists of blocks (the cache contents, in any order) and whose labels are cache events. Write $|C|$ for the length of a list $C$, $x :: C$ for $C$ with $x$ prepended, and $C \setminus v$ for $C$ with the first occurrence of $v$ removed. nodes.title: Legal cache transitions

Write $\mathrm{FIF}_k(R, C) = (E, D)$ when the furthest-in-future manager with capacity $k$ on the requests $R$ from the initial cache $C$ emits the events $E$ and ends with the cache $D$. Write $\mathrm{hit}(r)$ for a hit on $r$,…
nodes.title: One step of the furthest-in-future manager

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity, $R$ a list of requested blocks and $C$ a duplicate-free list of blocks of length at most $k$. Let $E$ be the events and $D$ the final cache produced by the furthest-in-future manager with capacity $k$ on $R$ from the initial cache $C$. Then $E$ leads from $C$ to $D$ by legal cache transitions for capacity $k$, the blocks requested by the events of $E$ are, in order, exactly $R$, and $D$ is…
nodes.title: The furthest-in-future manager produces legal traces

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity, $R$ a list of requested blocks and $C$ a duplicate-free list of blocks of length at most $k$. Let $E'$ be any list of cache events that leads from $C$ to some final cache by legal cache transitions for capacity $k$ and whose events request, in order, exactly the blocks of $R$. nodes.title: Optimality of furthest-in-future caching

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity, $R$ a list of requested blocks and $C$ a duplicate-free list of blocks of length at most $k$. Let $E'$ be any list of cache events that leads from $C$ to some final cache by legal cache transitions for capacity $k$ and whose events serve, in order, exactly the blocks of $R$. nodes.title: Furthest-in-future caching has the fewest misses

nodes.summary: For every capacity $k$ and every list $C$ of blocks, the furthest-in-future manager with capacity $k$ on the empty request list from the initial cache $C$ emits no events and ends with the cache $C$, unchanged.
nodes.title: Furthest-in-future on no requests

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity, $R$ a list of requested blocks and $C$ a duplicate-free list of blocks of length at most $k$. Then the events emitted by the furthest-in-future manager with capacity $k$ on $R$ from the initial cache $C$ serve, in order, exactly the blocks of $R$.
nodes.title: Furthest-in-future serves exactly the requests

nodes.summary: Run with capacity $0$ on a request sequence $r_1, \dots, r_n$ from the empty cache, the furthest-in-future manager emits exactly the events $\mathrm{miss}(r_1), \dots, \mathrm{miss}(r_n)$, one miss per request in order and each evicting no page, and its final cache is empty.
nodes.title: Furthest-in-future caching with zero capacity

nodes.summary: Given a capacity $k$, a sequence of requested pages and an initial cache (a list of pages), the furthest-in-future manager serves the requests in order and returns the list of emitted cache events together with the final cache. A request for a page $r$ already in the cache is a hit and leaves the cache unchanged. Otherwise it is a miss: if $k = 0$, nothing is evicted and the cache becomes empty; if the cache holds…
nodes.title: Furthest-in-future caching

nodes.summary: The miss indicator of a cache event is true if the event is a miss and false if it is a hit.
nodes.title: Miss indicator

nodes.summary: The number of misses of a finite list of cache events is the number of events in the list that are misses.
nodes.title: Number of misses in a trace

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity and $C$ a cache listing at most $k$ pages, and consider a legal trace of cache events for capacity $k$ that starts from $C$. Let $p$ be a page in $C$. If at least $k + 1$ distinct pages are each equal to $p$ or served by some event of the trace, then the trace contains at least one miss.
nodes.title: A legal trace misses at least once

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a capacity. If a legal trace of cache events for capacity $k$ starts from a cache $C$ and contains no miss, then every page served by an event of the trace lies in $C$.
nodes.title: A legal trace without misses serves only cached pages

nodes.summary: Let $k > 0$ be a capacity. If a legal transition for capacity $k$ takes a cache $C$ to a cache $C'$ by a cache event, then the page served by that event lies in $C'$.
nodes.title: A legal step caches the served page

nodes.summary: The page served by a cache event is the page it requests, whether the event is a hit or a miss.
nodes.title: Page served by a cache event

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
